Subject: Post-demo: commercial route selection & security gating — Avery Systems

Hi Jordan — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement and security can keep moving: 

Recap from today's call:
- Use case: internal search augmentation + re-ranking for support knowledge base; expected initial Q2 pilot ~100k tokens/day.
- Commercial routes discussed: Purchase Order (PO), credit card, or via cloud marketplace (preferred by some finance teams).
- Security/compliance asks: SOC 2 attestation, standard DPA, and a short questionnaire procurement runs for vendor onboarding.

Requested from your side:
1) Which payment path do you prefer (PO vs card vs marketplace)? If PO, please share the procurement contact and any PO template constraints.
2) Estimated start date for purchase / desired go-live (helps us prioritize slot on Dedicated pool).
3) Any required redlines in the DPA or special data residency notes?

Attachments: I attached a draft SOW and our most recent SOC 2 attestation for procurement to review. We'll also share a short vendor onboarding form for your procurement team to fill.

Next steps we propose (if that works on your end):
- You confirm payment path and procurement lead by 3/18.
- We return a redline-friendly DPA and invoice flow within 2 business days of confirmation.
- Marissa will coordinate marketplace options (if you prefer) and Ben will confirm billing emails/process.

If easier, we can loop your procurement contact into this thread — happy to jump on a short 20-min call with them.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Email: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.m@averysys.com>

Thanks Diego — great demo and clear recap. A few answers from procurement/security side: 

1) Payment preference: we prefer to use a standard PO. Finance will only use a marketplace purchase if it is significantly faster and the vendor's marketplace contract terms match our PO requirements.
2) Procurement lead: Alex Cho (cc'd) will own the PO. Alex — can you confirm the PO routing and any required fields?
3) Security gating: procurement requires SOC 2 (type II acceptable) and a DPA. They also have a short security questionnaire (I attached our vendor_assessment.xlsx) that we'll send for completion.

Timeline: Procurement expects to review contracts and vendor docs by 2027-03-25. If we can provide the SOC2 doc and a DPA draft by EOD 3/16, that should keep us on track.

We can start a pilot on a credit-card-backed test account if that helps get data flowing faster while PO paperwork completes — but longer-term they will bind the contract to a PO.

Jordan
Director, IT Procurement
